propositions: Lizard and jscpd adapter outputs are not wired into registered code_health metrics, leaving adapters as dead code despite working implementations.
Each metrics evaluation may invoke the same external analyzer (scc, lizard, jscpd) multiple times across registered metric specs, creating redundant executions.
Missing analyzer tools yield generic no-data or exception strings instead of honest Unavailable reasons naming the specific missing producer.
Complexity and duplication metrics must be registered and exposed alongside scc-derived LOC metrics, with per-context caching to ensure at most one execution per analyzer per metrics invocation.

Python and Go interface tests must validate loc, complexity, and duplication values through the real metrics entry point when tools are available, with clear Unavailable entries when producers are absent.
